key_insight: The nonlinear entropy-stable extension of Navier–Stokes–Fourier forms a fourth-order quasi-cubic system in entropy variables, while a quasi-linear approximation preserves its highest-order terms and entropy stability.
engineering_relevance: The closure offers a promising continuum-model route to improved rarefied-gas heat-transfer predictions beyond standard Navier–Stokes–Fourier equations.
method: Reformulate the extension in entropy variables using an inverse collision-operator derivative identity.
Apply the quasi-linear approximation to stationary heat transfer between parallel plates.
Analyze plane-wave dispersion for the one-dimensional linearized equations.
evidence_signal: Parallel-plate temperature profiles agree better with DSMC and heat flux agrees better with Sherman–Lees than the stated Navier–Stokes–Fourier comparisons; all modes in the linearized dispersion analysis are stable.
watch_item: The heat-transfer improvement relies on boundary conditions interpolating between continuum and collisionless limits, and the reported tests do not establish performance in complex multidimensional flows.
paper_title: Extensions to the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations for Rarefied Transport: Entropy Variable Formulation, Heat Transfer and Dispersion of a Non-Linear Entropy Stable Closure
